summary: Agent implemented the checkbox directly (Bash ls, Read index.html, one Edit) with no clarifying questions and no brainstorming skill invocation.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria met per session-log ground truth and screen output; the checkbox is present in coding-agent-workdir/index.html.

observations.description: coding-agent-token-usage.json (the headline cost artifact for this scenario) does not exist in the results directory after the run; `ls` of the run dir shows only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json. Cost measurement may depend on a later harness step.
Launching required four interactive confirmation prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions) before any work could start; both trust dialogs default to 'No, exit'.
Agent's final message notes 'No tests were run — the repo has no test setup', which is helpful and appropriately brief for a trivial change.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Plain static page, no framework or build. A basic form control is a single self-contained edit, so I'll just add it." followed by Update(index.html) adding `<input type="checkbox"> Done`; worked for 17s. Session-log tool_use list is exactly [Bash, Read, Edit].

jq over the rollout jsonl for assistant tool_use entries returned only ["Bash"],["Read"],["Edit"]; `grep -o 'superpowers:[a-z-]*'` on the log returned no matches (empty output). 'brainstorming' appears only as prose/skill-catalog text, no Skill tool call.
